rationale: C08 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template: both are presidential letters inviting governors collectively to a specifically scheduled conference, identifying its location and purpose, and closing with a courteous expression of hope that the recipient can attend. The child compresses and adapts that same structure to the narrower dust-storm emergency. C05 also concerns a governors' conference but primarily requests state delegations, while C22 requests a select group of governors to undertake a foreign visit and report back.

shared_material.child_excerpt: You are invited, along with Governors of other seriously affected states, to attend in the Cabinet Room of the White House a conference to discuss this problem at 2:30 p.m. April 26, 1954.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I extend to you and the Governors of the other States of the nation a most cordial invitation to attend a conference here in the White House on May fourth and fifth, for the purpose of participating in confidential discussions
shared_material.explanation: Both use the same invitation machinery: the recipient and other governors are invited to a White House conference on specified dates for discussion of identified problems.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I am hopeful that you will find it possible to be present.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I hope very much you will be able to join with me ... I trust you can be with us on these days.
shared_material.explanation: The closing attendance request uses closely parallel language and performs the same function.
